answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost. A marble stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a meadow holds the rep...
